notes.title: Steam Deck - Verified!
notes.content:
I'm happy to announce that the game just received "Verified" compatibility status!

You might have noticed it went from "Unsupported" to "Playable" a while ago and I kept fixing things and after a few review rounds with Valve we're finally here!
It wasn't easy because the game was not designed with controller in mind so I had to get creative like virtual cursor and burger-making minigame controls. I think the experience on the Steam Deck is pretty good and relatively intuitive.

The game utilizes a full 16:10 aspect ratio for most of the time, but sex scenes are locked to 16:9 with black bars at the top and bottom of the screen.

PS: In theory, it should also play well on other handheld console devices running on Windows or Linux operating systems.

[h1]About using PlayStation controller[/h1]
To see PlayStation-style icons when using a PS controller, you should disable Steam Input.

Go to the settings [cog icon to the right], then "Properties...", go to "Controller", and in "Override for Slave Harem" select "Disable Steam Input". You can switch between controllers at any time - the game engine will handle the display of glyphs upon pressing a button.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150055/ce4a4aabd896a390b4df70f464db5bceb6fb2758.png[/img]
Steam Deck unit provided courtesy of Valve for testing and development.

notes.title: 1.2 - Full controller support and more!
notes.content:
You must upgrade to continue playing - I changed Steamworks settings and only this build is compatible.

1.2:
- added full controller support (including PlayStation glyphs!)
- added emoji font fallback
- added support for aspect ratios different than 16:9
- lowered complexity of sliding puzzles
- fixed load slot not displaying levels
- fixed game crash when placing burger on empty tray
- slight changes to button handling
- UI adjustments - some elements have been remade
- added Linux build
- Steamworks settings adjustments

The changes aim to add full Steam Deck compatibility.

The codebase and architecture of this game were awful to work with again.
Lots of mechanics were designed with a mouse in mind so it was tricky to get controller working. Especially burgers.
I've decided to add a virtual cursor in some places like menus because the layout was terrible to move around with the controller.

UI changes are not huge, mostly just readability adjustments and controller-style support.

Due to the nature of the original design, I don't mark the gamepad as a recommended device - it's just better with the mouse, the virtual cursor does the trick but it doesn't make for a smooth and intuitive control.

As always, let me know if you encounter any issues. While changes are not visual, there were several code adjustments or even replacements.

notes.title: Patch 1.04 / 30 September
notes.content:
This patch should hopefully fix the edge-cases of game crashing when dialogue should be played, occurring for example when reaching highest level or changing clothes.

It will force-overwrite session data, clearing dialogue position that for some reason did not reset as it should after the end of an event.

notes.content:
This version fixes an issue with game breaking on clothes change. This error was affecting only a few users, so most of you probably didn't feel it. I don't know what the cause was- Well, I do know, the save data was wonky, but I don't know how it happened, my guess is... clicking too fast past dialogue and the system didn't register it properly. Anyway, the fix is rather crude and technically ugly, but it works if you have save affected by this.

In other news, I added a "Hide UI" button to sex scenes. You could have hidden it with the middle mouse button but apparently, a visual on-screen button is more obvious.

You can now check the version number on the "Credits" page from the main menu (panel displays on the right). Should state 1.03 under the title.

I hope that's all for this game and I can focus on the next ones. If you happen to encounter anything else, just let me know!

notes.title: About bugs and how to report them
notes.content:
The game still might have a few edge-cases bugs (a rare occurrence) and I've seen messages like "There's an error", "Can't progress" and similar without any details that would be useful to me to fix the problem.

As you can see, the game has several layers that interact with one another and you have plenty of agency how to progress the game. Some combinations might cause an error I was unable to catch during my testing before release.

[b]To make my work easier and your experience with the game better, please:[/b]
1) check if the issue was already reported in Community Hub ( https://steamcommunity.com/app/3136020/discussions/ ), if not, please make a new thread with a descriptive title (eg. Empty dialogue when [what?] )
2) please describe when error occurred, what you clicked immediately before it happened
3) check in the folder at %APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\My Cheetah Friend\logs if there's anything, it might help determine what caused the error, the log might have print something.
4) look in folder [%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\My Cheetah Friend] and send *.sav files to address:

artoonu [at] protonmail [dot] com


[b]For the black screen with music on start some users report:[/b]
- This seems to be an issue related to GPU drivers or settings and I cannot replicate it on my end. What I found online is that the game engine has issues when certain graphical features are forced via graphic global settings
You can try:
0) press "F11" or "F" on keyboard, it's a shortcut to switch between fullscreen and windowed mode which refreshes renderer
1) reinstall the game, restart the system
2) update the drivers, repeat 1
3) disable global graphic settings or revert them to default, repeat 1

----------

notes.title: Day 0 Patch
notes.content:
As you noticed, this kind of game has several various systems and it's cobbled together with duct tape and hopes. (In seriousness, it's quite a fancy system I designed from scratch).

As such, bugs are unfortunately possible, but I see your feedback and try to fix it ASAP. I do my best to minimize errors, but while testing, I often check something, then change a small portion of code later and assume that I didn't break that small thing... but it happened in this case.

This quick patch fixes and/or changes the following:
- missing references to scenes after purchasing sex gadgets causing pink screen and test line
- more "proper" window management, which should start as half of your resolution by default on the center of the native monitor instead of a predefined setting
- disabled debug mode (I think)
- updated engine version. While this might bring issues on its own, it should make the game more stable and from my quick testing I didn't find game-breaking issues, but keep me posted

As for the progression error two users reported, I cannot replicate it and don't know the cause of it yet. My guess is clicking too fast thus not registering events properly, but I don't know how to solve it yet.

If there are more issues, let me know! The best way would be to write in Community Hub as I get notification for each post - https://steamcommunity.com/app/3136020
